text:
maria: perf-ci alert on euw2-h100 smoke: p95 token latency jumped to ~780ms (baseline ~310ms). Noticed right after the 2026-03-17 runtime merges. :warning:

perf-ci: [ALERT] job=smoke-euw2-h100 perf_threshold breach. details: https://ci.internal/redwood/perf/1772345

jin: I pulled the smoke logs. KV cache eviction rate spiked ~4x at 12:02 UTC. KV miss traffic to origin also increased.

sophie: Any network spikes? ECMP churn?

samir: Yes, net counters on node euw2-h100-n12 show TX queue depths increasing and a few network retransmits around the same time. Suspect non-P2P memcpy path triggered by new kernel selection.

alex: What merge landed? I see commit `8f3a2b4` changed kernel selection heuristics for long sequences and also touched batch-packing logic.

maria: can we bisect quickly? CI green before this window.

jin: I ran a local bisect across the last 5 merges. The regression reproduces when `8f3a2b4` is present. Without it p95 goes back to ~320ms.

sophie: Repro script I used:```bash
# reproduce locally
export REDWOOD_CLUSTER=euw2-h100
./tools/perf_smoke --concurrency 16 --seq-dist long --run-duration 300
# sample outputs parsed by `jq`
```

samir: Profiling flamegraph (sampled) attached in gist: https://gist.internal/fg/abc123 - shows a higher proportion of time in `memcpy_host_to_device` path and kernel fallback `generic_gemm` during long sequences.

alex: That aligns: commit `8f3a2b4` added a heuristic to avoid certain fused kernels for sequences > 2048 tokens, supposed to reduce OOM risk, but seems to cause worse kernel selection for H100 (nvlink/p2p) path leading to extra host <-> device copies.

perf-ci: CI job `smoke-euw2-h100` failed on 2026-03-17T12:05 with p95=780ms. Triggered by merged PR #3124 (8f3a2b4).

maria: Is it only H100? I didn't see the same severity on A10/L4 clusters.

jin: On L4/A10 we see a tiny bump but caches absorb it. H100 had higher KV cache eviction rate because batching reduced effective prefix reuse and kernel fallback introduced copies that evicted KV entries faster.

sophie: Also saw ECMP pathing shift: packets for some flows went over a different nic leading to increased latency for a subset of hosts (noisy neighbor effect). The kernel change increased small-burst network traffic pattern.

samir: Reproduce logs (trimmed):```text
[12:02:03] kvcache: evict_rate=0.041 -> 0.17
[12:02:04] kernel_select: chosen=fallback_generic_gemm reason="heuristic-long-seq"
[12:02:04] net: txq_overflow=12 retransmits=5
[12:02:05] perf: p95_tokens=780ms
```

alex: Action plan: hold rollout for euw2-h100 and rollback PR #3124 until we have a targeted fix. I can open a revert PR.

maria: Please add a rollout hold in console and pause canaries: `PATCH /api/rollouts/hold?cluster=euw2-h100&tag=2026-03-17`

deploy-bot: `rollout hold` executed for cluster=euw2-h100 by alex at 2026-03-17T12:20Z :white_check_mark:

jin: I'll prepare a minimal repro and a test that asserts KV eviction delta < 2x for smoke workloads. Putting a perf gate in CI.

sophie: Also recommend we add a targeted test for H100 that verifies we prefer nvlink/p2p kernel paths and assert against extra host memcpy.

samir: For immediate mitigation, can we force kernel selection flag `--force-p2p` on euw2-h100 pool? Might be a quick toggle.

alex: We should avoid cluster-specific hacks unless temporary. I'll revert the heuristic and add a follow-up PR with config toggles + better detection of p2p availability. Revert PR: `git revert 8f3a2b4 -m 1` -> PR #3130.

maria: Great. Once revert lands, run the smoke job and re-run bisect script to confirm. If green, proceed with a careful canary with traffic shaping to catch ECMP effects.

perf-ci: follow-up: smoke-euw2-h100 after revert: p95=318ms (baseline 310ms) - regression resolved in staging run 1772350.

alex: Keeping rollout on hold until we validate full canary and add H100-specific test. I'll also ask infra to check for any NIC firmware updates that could interact with our memcpy patterns.

sophie: filing a post-merge checklist item: when kernel selection heuristics touch fallback paths, run cross-hardware perf matrix (H100/A10/L4) and KV cache pressure sim.

maria: thanks all. assigning owners: jin (perf test), alex (revert & canary), samir (profiling), sophie (testing matrix).

alex: cc @oncall if anything odd pops back up. :eyes:
